items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Jeff...what do you call it, Jeff Holloway. Do you remember that?

ctx.x: out in the morning, come back in. Jeff...what do you call it, Jeff Holloway. Do you remember that? The L&M Indian out there? And you'd go up to the IC, and you'd see the station, people...people well-dressed... You'd see people happy and well-dressed, not people sad, going to some towns in Georgia and Mississippi, the little small towns. And you'd see everybody relaxed, you know.

The late Arthur Stanley called New Orleans the Metropolitan City. And I got to understand what that means. It's not all White and Black Baptists, like you would go into Beaufort, Georgia or something, or you were going to Calverton(?), Alabama, or somewhere in Mississippi, where all the people... And there's two people -- White and Black. Because you have to always observe that when you're playing music, who you're playing for and what kind of music to play for them, and how to please and satisfy these people.
